propositions: Full-state snapshot cadence with fixed threshold (T=10) creates superlinear Θ(N²) retained snapshot bytes because each fold embeds the complete growing state and retires all prior snapshots append-only, never deleted.

Byte/replay-cost-aware cadence (fold when pending_source_bytes >= alpha * active_snapshot_bytes) reduces retained snapshot bytes to Θ(N) with amplification factor ≈ 1/alpha and bounds replay cost to alpha fraction of snapshot load.

The cadence change modifies only the needs_folding trigger predicate; all ADR-0035 invariants (conservative horizon, rebuild-on-stray, crash recovery, two-clone union merge) are preserved because snapshot placement, source_event_uuids, retire/restore, and replay ordering remain unchanged.

Benchmark measurement at N=8,000 events shows control policy yields 5.3 GB retired bytes (344× reduction achieved with alpha=1.0: 15.6 MB) while keeping snapshot count low but tail replay time unbounded.
Mixed-version rollback and forward compatibility require the new snapshot_alpha config default to <= 0 (inert), making the change a pure no-op until explicitly opted in.
